answer: One concrete defense is a non-transferable stake locked before an agent earns credit. Each identity posts a bond larger than any single reward, held per identity rather than per owner, so ten thousand fake agents need ten thousand separately funded bonds. Even a light zephyr of duplicate accounts must sink that capital and risk slashing. Withdrawals sit on a ledge of delay, blocking colluders from recycling funds across identities in one epoch. Each seat on the graded mesa carries its own collateral, so attacker cost scales linearly while legitimate yield stays flat.
